data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Assumes the log is complete and self-contained.","Ignores non-deterministic elements (e.g., timestamps, randomness)."],"overturn_conditions":["Evidence that the log includes non-deterministic elements.","Demonstration that the replay mechanism differs from the original execution environment."],"shared_structure":["Deterministic systems produce identical outputs for identical inputs.","Divergence implies a flaw in the system."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["If deterministic replay is possible, silent divergence becomes a contradiction."]},"claim":"Deterministic replay with a fixed initial state alone turns silent divergence into a contradiction, because any divergence implies the log or replay mechanism is flawed.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The log must be complete (no hidden external inputs).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The replay mechanism must be identical to the original execution environment.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The initial state must be fixed and immutable.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the log and replay mechanism are deterministic, any divergence between the published result and replayed log must be due to an error in the log or replay process, thus a contradiction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
